answer: At dawn each epoch, every new identity starts in a probationary haven: tiny trade caps that grow only after a history of honest deals. An agent's limit rises slowly with each clean settlement, like a ship earning a longer voyage after every safe return to port. A sybil farmer can mint a thousand keys, but each fake must wait out the same slow probation and complete real trades to gain any meaningful limit, so cloning buys no instant scale; the attacker's cost is time plus genuine work per fake, while one honest agent simply ages into full trust.
